cells.title: multi-hop, sanity: two facts told in different weeks and a question that names both - both are in the packet
cells.note: the positive control of the multi-hop scorer: a question that names a person and an appointment finds both facts when the store ranks by the query, and neither when search ignores it (the retrieval control)

cells.title: long-range associative recall: 20 questions that need TWO facts said weeks apart (is X's birthday before my dentist appointment / who in my family lives near Y's school), 100 household turns between and after - both facts are in the packet (>= 70%)
cells.note: 10 date comparisons and 10 place joins. A hit = the packet (the arm's associative recall, 8 rows) holds a row naming the subject and the answer token for the first fact AND for the second. The join questions name only the first fact's subject: the second fact is reachable only through the place the first one names, so a plain top-k over the question misses it where an associative step (Hindsight's link graph) finds it. The first fact is 14-28 days old, the second 1-9. MEASURED on the lab's Z0 (bag-of-words ranking + the service's 70-day recency decay): 3 of 20 at 100 filler, the joins 0 of 10 - an older fact loses to a newer near-miss, and the second fact of a join is never reached. A TARGET on Z0; Z0e (the same service over a real Chroma + MiniLM, the baseline an embedding arm is measured against) reaches 14 of 20: dates 10 of 10, joins 4 of 10 - the first fact is found, the second is not, which is the missing associative step
